<reason>CON won the motion as written: mandate plus real price control pull opposite ways, and PRO never showed how a captive buyer facing a small manufacturer set gets durable net-price discipline. CON better weighed scale, in-year versus delayed savings, and the risk of stacking drug spend on still-arriving complications. PRO was sharp on stigma and unpaid sequelae, but that did not rescue the value-based half. Clipped CON turns kept the margin competitive.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON collapsing PRO's outcomes contracts: the payoff shrank from avoided heart failure to in-year weight/glucose, those endpoints pay out routinely, and sellers can price responders to cover refunds once the buyer cannot walk away.</best_rebuttal>
